Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the Redwood team. A couple of quick clarifications from our side to help scope the pilot:
- Primary use case is streaming chat for our in-product assistant (low-latency responses while streaming partial answers).
- Typical request: ~150 concurrent active users at peak, ~180 tokens per request on average, burst to 300 concurrent sessions for 30s spikes.
- Target: p95 end-to-end latency for first tokens under 300ms, steady-state token generation latency ideally <80ms/token for streaming.
- Important: cost target of <$0.0025 per generated token for the steady-state workload (we know this is rough).

I attached a small set of anonymized traces and a short doc with session patterns. Can Redwood run a pilot that shows tradeoffs (batching, KV caching, quantization) and recommended model variant(s)?

Appreciate a suggested next step and a proposed scope for a 2-week perf pilot.

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for the traces. Helpful. High level response and proposed plan below.

Quick read on feasibility: we can meet the streaming-first p95 target with a combination of (A) continuous batching tuned to the session arrival characteristics, (B) prefix/KV caching for repeated context, and (C) a quantized model variant for the steady-state path.

Proposed 2-week pilot scope (summary):
1) Performance validation lab: Redwood runs your traces against two model variants (float16 baseline, 4-bit quantized variant) under three config profiles: low-latency (minimal batching), cost-optimized (larger batch windows + KV cache), and hybrid (adaptive batching + cache).
2) Streaming instrumentation: capture p50/p95 token latency, time-to-first-token, throughput (tokens/s), and GPU utilization.
3) Concurrency burn: simulate 150 steady concurrent users + 3x burst windows to validate autoscaling/fallback.
4) Cost projection: modeled token unit economics per profile plus recommendations for model and routing policy.
5) Deliverable: concise report, suggested production config, and an MAP with milestones for a pilot -> production rollout.

Immediate asks from us to you:
- Confirm target p95 <= 300ms (first-token) and your strictest cost per-token target.
- Re-send trace samples if possible with a few more long-tail sessions ( >800 tokens ).
- Availability for a 30–45 min kickoff next Tue or Wed (we'll need SRE on the call).

Next steps we recommend on Redwood side: Ben will draft an initial config matrix (batch windows, KV cache TTLs, quantization profile choices) and Priyom will propose a naïve cost model so you have a pricing floor for each profile.

Sofia / Alex — I sketched out concrete levers we should try in the lab. Notes below are meant to be short hand for the config matrix Ben will include in the MAP.

1) Batching strategy
  - Low-latency: 8ms batch accumulation window, dynamic early flush at 75 tokens (expected p95 first-token ~220–280ms depending on model).
  - Cost-optimized: 30ms window + micro-batches of 4 requests; expect ~2–3x token cost savings vs low-latency at the expense of added tail latency during bursts.
  - Hybrid/adaptive: start with 8ms, widen to 20–30ms when queue depth exceeds threshold (keeps p50 tight while limiting cost in steady state).

2) KV/prefix caching
  - TTL choices: 30s, 5min, 1hr — we'll test cache hit rates (your traces suggest ~40% repeated context within 2min). Even 30s TTL can cut tokens generated by 15–25% on some conversation patterns.

3) Quantization profiles
  - Baseline FP16
  - 8-bit dynamic quantization for latency-friendly path (small memory reduction, minimal quality loss)
  - 4-bit GPTQ-style profile for cost-optimized runs (noted ~1.5–2x throughput improvement in our lab on similar models; quality checks needed).

4) Model routing / fallback
  - Primary: quantized variant for steady-state traffic
  - Fallback: FP16 for low-latency or for requests flagged by evals to require higher fidelity

Preliminary cost ranges (very rough):
  - Low-latency profile: ~$0.0038–0.0045 per token equivalent (higher GPU utilization, lower batch efficiency)
  - Cost-optimized profile: ~$0.0018–0.0026 per token equivalent (depends on cache hit rate and quantization quality)

I'll deliver the detailed matrix and a simple simulation script we can run against your traces. Priyom, can you produce an initial cost projection table by EOD tomorrow?

—Ben
